source.title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space

accepted.question_text: Let D be the open unit disk in the complex plane, let dS be normalized area measure on D, and let L^2_a(D) be the Bergman space of analytic functions on D with finite integral of |f|^2 against dS. A closed subspace J of L^2_a(D) is z-invariant when zf belongs to J for every f in J. Characterize all z-invariant closed subspaces of L^2_a(D).
accepted.context_brief: Invariant subspaces of the Bergman shift

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1 Characterize the invariant subspaces of L2a(D).

accepted.question_text: Let D be the open unit disk and L^2_a(D) the Bergman space of square-area-integrable analytic functions on D. A sequence A of points in D is an L^2_a(D) zero sequence when some function in L^2_a(D) vanishes precisely on A, counting multiplicities. Characterize exactly which sequences in D are zero sequences for L^2_a(D).

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 2 Characterize the L2a(D) zero sequences.

accepted.question_text: For the Bergman space L^2_a(D) on the open unit disk, find an effective factorization theory for its functions, analogous in usefulness to the Hardy-space factorization into Blaschke products, singular inner functions, and outer functions.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 3 Find an effective factorization of the functions in L2a(D).

accepted.question_text: For an inner divisor phi in L^2_a(D), let Phi_phi be the potential associated with phi, satisfying Delta Phi_phi = |phi|^2 - 1 in D and vanishing on the boundary circle, with the boundary gradient condition used for inner divisors. The known isometry for f in H^2(D) is ||phi f||^2_L2 = ||f||^2_L2 + integral_D |f'(z)|^2 Phi_phi(z) dS(z). Determine precisely for which inner divisors phi this isometry extends to every f in L^2_a(D), allowing the value +infinity on both sides.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 4 Does the isometry (2.1) in Theorem 2.4 extend

accepted.question_text: For a finite zero divisor phi in the Bergman space L^2_a(D), let Gamma_|phi|^2(z,zeta) be the Green function for the weighted fourth-order operator Delta_z |phi(z)|^(-2) Delta_z on D with Dirichlet and gradient-zero boundary conditions. Is the exterior normal derivative partial_n Delta_z Gamma_|phi|^2(z,zeta) nonnegative for every boundary point z on the unit circle and every interior point zeta in D?
accepted.context_brief: Boundary positivity for weighted biharmonic Green functions

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 4.2 For a finite zero divisor phi

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be finite zero sequences in D with A contained in B, and let phi_A and phi_B be their associated Bergman zero divisors. Does the argument of the quotient phi_B(z)/phi_A(z) increase monotonically as z travels counterclockwise around the unit circle? In the special case where B differs from A by one point, is phi_B/phi_A a star-shaped univalent function on D?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 4.3 Let A, B be two finite zero divisors

accepted.question_text: Let omega be a positive C-infinity smooth weight on the closed unit disk that reproduces the origin for bounded harmonic functions, meaning h(0) = integral_D h(z) omega(z) dS(z). Suppose omega satisfies Delta log omega(z) >= -1/(1 - |z|^2)^2 in D. Is the Green function Gamma_omega(z,zeta) for the weighted biharmonic operator Delta omega^(-1) Delta positive on D x D?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 4.4 Let omega be a positive C-infinity-smooth weight

accepted.question_text: Let A be a zero sequence for L^2_a(D), let phi_A be the zero divisor associated with A, and let I(A) be the invariant subspace of functions in L^2_a(D) that vanish on A. Does phi_A generate I(A) as an invariant subspace, equivalently do phi_A, z phi_A, z^2 phi_A, and so on span a dense subspace of I(A)?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 5 Does phi_A generate I(A)
This problem was solved

accepted.question_text: Let A be a Bergman zero sequence in D, let phi_A be its zero divisor, and let phi_{A union {0}} be the zero divisor obtained after adding a zero at the origin. Is the quotient phi_{A union {0}}/phi_A always a bounded analytic function on D?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded quotient after adding one zero

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 6 Is the function phi_A union {0}/phi_A always bounded
solved in the affirmative

accepted.question_text: Let omega be a continuous nonnegative function on D such that omega(z) <= C(1 - |z|^2) for some positive constant C and omega is super-biharmonic, Delta^2 omega >= 0 in D. Are analytic polynomials dense in the weighted Bergman space L^2_a(D,omega) consisting of analytic functions f on D with integral_D |f(z)|^2 omega(z) dS(z) finite?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 7 Suppose omega is a continuous function on D
Problem 7 as stated above has an affirmative answer

accepted.question_text: Let f be analytic on D and suppose that integral_D h(z)|f(z)|^2 dS(z) <= h(0) for every positive bounded harmonic function h on D. Must f be the normal limit, meaning uniform convergence on compact subsets of D, of finite zero divisors for the Bergman space?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 6.2 Suppose f is analytic on D
settled affirmatively

accepted.question_text: Let M(H^2,L^2_a) be the multiplier space from the Hardy space H^2(D) to the Bergman space L^2_a(D), with norm sup ||phi f||_L2 over ||f||_H2 <= 1. Is every inner divisor for L^2_a(D) approximable by zero divisors in the M(H^2,L^2_a) norm?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 8 Is every inner divisor for L2a(D)
no progress on this problem

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant epsilon with 0 < epsilon < 2^(-1/2) such that, whenever f and g belong to L^2_a(D) and |f(z)| <= |g(z)| throughout the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, it follows that ||f||_L2 <= ||g||_L2?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 8.1 (Korenblum) There exists an absolute constant epsilon
Conjecture 8.1 was settled

accepted.question_text: For f,g in L^2_a(D), write f precedes g in the Korenblum domination order when ||fh||_L2 <= ||gh||_L2 for every bounded analytic h on D. If f precedes g and g precedes f, must f be equal to gamma g for some unimodular constant gamma?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 9 Suppose f, g in L2a(D)
solved this problem in the affirmative

accepted.question_text: A function f in L^2_a(D) is cyclic when the functions f, zf, z^2 f, and so on span a dense subspace of L^2_a(D). Describe exactly which elements of L^2_a(D) are cyclic.
accepted.context_brief: Cyclic vectors in the Bergman space

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 10 Describe the cyclic elements of L2a(D).

accepted.question_text: Let A^-infinity be the algebra of analytic functions on D satisfying a growth bound |f(z)| <= C(1 - |z|^2)^(-N) for some positive constants C and N. If f belongs to L^2_a(D) and is cyclic in A^-infinity, meaning it generates a dense ideal there, must f also be cyclic in L^2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 11 (Korenblum)
Does the converse hold

accepted.question_text: Suppose f belongs to L^2_a(D) and satisfies a lower growth bound |f(z)| >= epsilon (1 - |z|^2)^N throughout D for some positive constants epsilon and N. Must f be cyclic in L^2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 12 (Shapiro)
settled in the negative

accepted.question_text: For two disjoint Bergman zero sequences A and B, let I(A) and I(B) be the invariant subspaces of functions in L^2_a(D) that vanish on A and B respectively, and let M be the closed linear span of I(A) and I(B). The index of an invariant subspace M is dim(M/zM). Determine exactly for which pairs A,B the subspace M has index 1.
accepted.context_brief: Index of spans of two zero-based subspaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 13 Determine for which pairs of disjoint zero sequences

accepted.question_text: Determine which Bergman zero sequences A have the property that every z-invariant subspace M of L^2_a(D) containing I(A), the functions that vanish on A, has index 1.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 14 Determine the zero sequences A

accepted.question_text: Determine which functions f in L^2_a(D) have the property that every z-invariant subspace of L^2_a(D) containing f has index 1, where the index of an invariant subspace M is dim(M/zM).

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 15 Determine which f in L2a(D)

accepted.question_text: A z-invariant subspace I of L^2_a(D) is maximal when every invariant subspace containing I is either I or the whole space. Must every maximal invariant subspace of L^2_a(D) have codimension 1?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 16 Must every maximal invariant subspace
answered in the affirmative

accepted.question_text: Let M be a z-invariant subspace of L^2_a(D). Suppose N is another z-invariant subspace contained in M and maximal among proper invariant subspaces contained in M. Must N have codimension 1 inside M?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 17 Let M be an invariant subspace

accepted.question_text: Let mu be a positive measure on D such that point evaluation on polynomials is bounded and mu reproduces the origin, integral_D p(z) dmu(z) = p(0) for all polynomials p. Let P^2(mu) be the closure of polynomials in L^2(mu), and define the Cauchy dual as the analytic functions whose boundary Cauchy pairing gives bounded linear functionals on P^2(mu). Is the reproducing kernel of the Cauchy dual of P^2(mu) always a complete Nevanlinna-Pick kernel?
accepted.context_brief: Cauchy dual kernels for nonradial measures

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 18 Let mu be a measure as above

accepted.question_text: Let omega be a logarithmically subharmonic weight on D that reproduces the origin. Is the reproducing kernel k of the weighted Bergman space L^2_a(D,omega) a Bergman-type kernel, meaning a reproducing kernel of the McCullough-Richter form k(z,lambda) = (1 - conjugate(psi(lambda)) psi(z))^(-1)(1 - v(z,lambda)) for an analytic psi with psi(0)=0 and psi'(0) nonzero and a positive definite kernel v with v(0,0)=0?
accepted.context_brief: Bergman-type kernels for logarithmically subharmonic weights

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 19 Let omega be a logarithmically subharmonic weight
problem is still open

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH resolver URL with document id 2226539.

Queried the official zbMATH API. Metadata identified Zbl 1082.30025, the title Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space, authors Alexandru Aleman, Hakan Hedenmalm, and Stefan Richter, and pages 27-59 in Operator Theory: Advances and Applications 156. The API links field was empty, so metadata was used only for identity recovery.

Recovered an author-hosted readable PDF of the same exact work at KTH. A direct shell download failed with DNS resolution for people.kth.se, so extraction used the readable PDF text exposed by the browser/page-reading tool.

Mapped sections 1-12. Open-question regions were found in the basic project, inner-divisor isometry, potential theory, generators of zero-based subspaces, Caratheodory and Frostman analogues, Korenblum maximum principle, cyclic vectors, index, maximal invariant subspaces, and reproducing-kernel methods.
Extracted Problems 1-4 from the basic project and inner-divisor isometry discussion.
Extracted Conjectures 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4 from the weighted biharmonic Green-function section.
Extracted Problems 5-8 and Conjecture 6.2; solved-status markers were recorded for Problems 5-7 and Conjecture 6.2.
Extracted Conjecture 8.1 and Problems 9-12 from the Korenblum and cyclic-vector sections; solved-status markers were recorded for Conjecture 8.1 and Problems 9 and 12.
Extracted Problems 13-19 from the sections on index, maximal invariant subspaces, and reproducing kernels; solved-status marker was recorded for Problem 16.

Expanded all extracted statements into standalone questions by inlining the relevant definitions of D, L^2_a(D), invariant subspace, zero sequence, inner divisor, Korenblum domination, cyclicity, index, Cauchy dual, and Bergman-type kernel where needed.
No near-duplicate questions were merged. Earlier broad projects and later narrower subproblems were kept separate because their scopes differ.

Accepted all extracted items after checking self-containedness, source adequacy, solved-status metadata, and schema conformance. Evidence quotes are concise anchors to the labeled source statements and solved-status labels.
Saved JSON to outputs/parse-paper/2226539.json and outputs/latest.json.
